question_text: A steel contains $18 \%$ pearlite and $82 \%$ primary ferrite at room temperature. Estimate the carbon content of the steel.The unit of the answer is %.
response:
Using the lever rule on the Fe–Fe₃C phase diagram:

The pearlite fraction equals the mass fraction of austenite just above the eutectoid that transformed. With the eutectoid composition $C_{\text{eut}} \approx 0.76\%$ C and the ferrite composition at the eutectoid $C_\alpha \approx 0.022\%$ C:

$$f_{\text{pearlite}} = \frac{C_0 - C_\alpha}{C_{\text{eut}} - C_\alpha}$$

$$0.18 = \frac{C_0 - 0.022}{0.76 - 0.022}$$

$$C_0 = 0.022 + 0.18(0.738) \approx 0.155\%$$

$$\boxed{0.155}$$
